claim: The co-translational regulation of RPL3 and RPL4 mRNA levels represents an elegant mechanism to specifically reduce the de novo synthesis of Rpl3 and Rpl4 when their unassembled levels exceed the buffering capacity of the dedicated chaperones Rrb1 and Acl4.
source: Accordingly, the here-described co-translational regulation of RPL3 and RPL4 mRNA levels represents an elegant mechanism to specifically reduce the de novo synthesis of Rpl3 and Rpl4 when their unassembled levels exceed, due to a perturbation of ribosome assembly, the buffering capacity of the dedicated chaperones Rrb1 and Acl4.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the functional significance of the regulatory mechanism.

claim: The regulatory mechanism continuously operates under normal growth conditions.
source: While the above would suggest a special relevance for rapidly responding to certain stress conditions, our data indicate that the regulatory mechanism also continuously operates under normal growth conditions.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the data showing regulation occurs even without stress.

claim: The RPL3 and RPL4A/B transcripts are among the five RPG mRNAs exhibiting markedly shorter half-lives than all other RPG mRNAs.
source: In line with a constant adjustment of their transcript levels via a regulated degradation pathway, the RPL3 and RPL4A/B transcripts are among the five RPG mRNAs exhibiting markedly shorter half-lives than all other RPG mRNAs (Wang et al., 2002).
evidence: This is a statement about mRNA half-lives, citing Wang et al., 2002.

claim: Both Rpl3 and Rpl4 are among the earliest assembling large subunit r-proteins, associating shortly before or after the generation of the 27SA2 pre-rRNA.
source: Both Rpl3 and Rpl4, by associating shortly before or after the generation of the 27SA2 pre-rRNA, are among the earliest assembling large subunit r-proteins, and they fulfill a central role for the compaction and/or stabilization of the earliest pre-60S particles (Rosado et al., 2007; Pöll et al., 2009; Gamalinda et al., 2014; Pillet et al., 2015; Joret et al., 2018).
evidence: This describes the timing and importance of Rpl3 and Rpl4 assembly, citing five references.

claim: Rpl3 and Rpl4 fulfill a central role for the compaction and/or stabilization of the earliest pre-60S particles.
source: Both Rpl3 and Rpl4, by associating shortly before or after the generation of the 27SA2 pre-rRNA, are among the earliest assembling large subunit r-proteins, and they fulfill a central role for the compaction and/or stabilization of the earliest pre-60S particles (Rosado et al., 2007; Pöll et al., 2009; Gamalinda et al., 2014; Pillet et al., 2015; Joret et al., 2018).
evidence: This describes the functional role of Rpl3 and Rpl4 in ribosome assembly, citing five references.

claim: The temporary nuclear storage of Rpl3 and Rpl4 in complex with their dedicated chaperone provides the required buffering capacity to rapidly respond to short-term increases in assembly demand.
source: The temporary nuclear storage of Rpl3 and Rpl4 in complex with their dedicated chaperone not only provides the required buffering capacity to rapidly respond to short-term increases in assembly demand but also the means to relay and directly connect the status of early pre-60S assembly to the rate of the two r-proteins' de novo synthesis.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the functional significance of chaperone-mediated storage.

claim: The temporary nuclear storage of Rpl3 and Rpl4 in complex with their dedicated chaperone provides the means to relay and directly connect the status of early pre-60S assembly to the rate of the two r-proteins' de novo synthesis.
source: The temporary nuclear storage of Rpl3 and Rpl4 in complex with their dedicated chaperone not only provides the required buffering capacity to rapidly respond to short-term increases in assembly demand but also the means to relay and directly connect the status of early pre-60S assembly to the rate of the two r-proteins' de novo synthesis.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the functional significance of chaperone-mediated storage.

claim: Compared to a purely transcription-based adaptation of protein levels, the uncovered regulatory mechanism has the advantage of enabling a more rapid response.
source: Compared to a purely transcription-based adaptation of protein levels, the uncovered regulatory mechanism, owing to the constant supply of new RPL3 and RPL4A/B mRNAs that are then either translated or subjected to regulated degradation, has the evident advantage of enabling a more rapid response.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the advantages of the regulatory mechanism.

claim: The accurate functioning of the regulatory system is instrumental to avoid the impact of both the surplus and insufficient supply of Rpl3 and/or Rpl4.
source: We conclude that the accurate functioning of this regulatory system is instrumental to avoid the impact of both the surplus and insufficient supply of Rpl3 and/or Rpl4.
evidence: This is a conclusion about the importance of the regulatory system.

claim: An involvement of one of the associated core components of the Ccr4-Not complex in mRNA degradation can be supposed.
source: Considering the mandatory requirement of a physical connection with Not1 for negative regulation of RPL3 and RPL4 mRNA levels to occur, an involvement of one of the associated core components of the Ccr4-Not complex can be supposed.
evidence: This is a speculation about which components mediate mRNA degradation.

claim: It is highly likely that the Caf1-Ccr4 deadenylase module promotes degradation of the RPL3 and RPL4 mRNA.
source: Since it is well established that the Ccr4-Not complex plays an important role in the decay of cytoplasmic mRNAs, a process that is initiated by deadenylation of the poly(A) tail (Parker, 2012), we consider it highly likely that its Caf1-Ccr4 deadenylase module promotes degradation of the RPL3 and RPL4 mRNA.
evidence: This is a speculation about the mechanism of mRNA degradation, citing Parker, 2012.

claim: The utilization of a defined segment of the encoded nascent polypeptide constitutes an unprecedented mechanism of recruitment of the Ccr4-Not complex to a substrate mRNA.
source: Notably, the utilization of a defined segment of the encoded nascent polypeptide constitutes, to the best of our knowledge, an unprecedented mechanism of recruitment of the Ccr4-Not complex to a substrate mRNA, which is more conventionally achieved through interactions with either the poly(A)-binding protein or rather general as well as specific RNA-binding proteins (Parker, 2012; Wahle and Winkler, 2013; Bresson and Tollervey, 2018), but, as recently shown, can also occur via the accommodation of the Not5-NTD in the ribosomal E-site of mRNAs displaying low codon optimality (Buschauer et al., 2020).
evidence: This is a statement about the novelty of the recruitment mechanism, citing four references.

claim: Heterodimeric NAC is involved in the substrate recognition process.
source: The strict requirement of both NAC subunits for negative regulation indicates that heterodimeric NAC, owing to its established role as a ribosome-associated chaperone that binds nascent chains (Deuerling et al., 2019), is involved in the substrate recognition process.
evidence: This is an inference from the genetic requirement for both NAC subunits, citing Deuerling et al., 2019.

claim: The yeast NAC-β subunits may be responsible for establishing the initial contact with the N-terminal part of the regulation-conferring segment of nascent Rpl3 and Rpl4.
source: Given that the N-terminal tail of NAC-β can insert, as seen in the cryo-EM structure of a reconstituted Caenorhabditis elegans NAC-60S complex, up to the constriction point of the polypeptide exit tunnel to sense and bind to nascent chains (Gamerdinger et al., 2019), we assume that the yeast NAC-β subunits may be responsible for establishing the initial contact with the N-terminal part of the regulation-conferring segment of nascent Rpl3 and Rpl4.
evidence: This is a speculation based on structural data from C. elegans, citing Gamerdinger et al., 2019.

claim: The residues following the key residues F16/L17 in Rpl3 and W109 in Rpl4 may have a propensity for stalling the nascent chain in the exit tunnel.
source: Conspicuously, in both cases the residues identified as being crucial for conferring regulation, F16/L17 and W109, respectively, are followed by a segment of around 30 amino acids that is also required to confer maximal regulation. Considering that around 25–30 amino acids are generally buried within the exit tunnel (Bhushan et al., 2010; Wilson et al., 2016; Döring et al., 2017), we speculate that the residues following these key residues, especially those potentially extending from the constriction point of the tunnel to the peptidyl transferase center, may have a propensity for stalling the nascent chain in the exit tunnel.
evidence: This is a speculation based on the length of the exit tunnel, citing three references.

claim: Timely association with the dedicated chaperone may preclude NAC from interacting with nascent Rpl3 or Rpl4 and allow translation to proceed.
source: The immediate proximity or even partial overlap of the Rrb1- or Acl4-binding site and the key residues of the regulation-conferring segment suggests that timely association with the dedicated chaperone may preclude NAC from interacting with nascent Rpl3 or Rpl4 and allow translation to proceed.
evidence: This is a speculation based on the overlap of binding sites.

claim: If Rpl3 or Rpl4 are not swiftly captured by their dedicated chaperone, NAC could sense and bind to the regulation-conferring segment, an event that presumably fortifies stalling.
source: Conversely, if these are not swiftly enough captured by their dedicated chaperone, NAC could sense and bind to the regulation-conferring segment, an event that presumably fortifies stalling and, thereby, further decreases the speed of translation.
evidence: This is a speculation about the consequence of delayed chaperone binding.

claim: The findings are reminiscent of the observation that mammalian mRNAs encoding proteins whose signal sequence is inefficiently recognized by the signal recognition particle (SRP) are selectively degraded.
source: Moreover, our findings are reminiscent of the previous observation that mammalian mRNAs encoding proteins whose signal sequence is inefficiently recognized by the signal recognition particle (SRP) are, albeit by a yet to be determined mechanism, selectively degraded (Karamyshev et al., 2014).
evidence: This draws a parallel to a similar mechanism in mammalian cells, citing Karamyshev et al., 2014.

claim: The study highlights the r-proteins Rpl3 and Rpl4 as potential drivers of cellular protein aggregation.
source: Notably, our study highlights the r-proteins Rpl3 and Rpl4 as potential drivers of cellular protein aggregation.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the aggregation experiments.

claim: The aggregation of unassembled r-proteins represents a threat to the maintenance of cellular proteostasis.
source: Our findings therefore further reinforce the notion that the aggregation of unassembled r-proteins represents a threat to the maintenance of cellular proteostasis, which, as shown by previous studies, yeast cells try first to avoid by clearing excess r-proteins via Tom1-mediated degradation (ERISQ pathway) and then to resolve by activating a stress response pathway, referred to as RASTR or RPAS, that increases the protein folding, disaggregation, and degradation capacity and decreases Ifh1-dependent transcription of RPGs (Sung et al., 2016a; Albert et al., 2019; Tye et al., 2019).
evidence: This is a conclusion reinforced by the study's findings, citing three references.

claim: The reduced supply of single r-proteins, resulting in the accumulation of orphan r-proteins, causes proteotoxic stress and cell elimination in Drosophila.
source: Importantly, the reduced supply of single r-proteins, resulting in the accumulation of orphan r-proteins, has also recently been shown to cause proteotoxic stress and cell elimination in Drosophila (Baumgartner et al., 2021; Recasens-Alvarez et al., 2021).
evidence: This cites recent findings in Drosophila, citing two references.

claim: Mutations in around 20 different RPGs, mostly leading to haploinsufficiency of individual r-proteins, result in the development of Diamond-Blackfan anemia (DBA).
source: Moreover, it is well established that mutations in around 20 different RPGs, mostly leading to haploinsufficiency of individual r-proteins, result in the development of a ribosomopathy called Diamond-Blackfan anemia (DBA) (Narla and Ebert, 2010; Danilova and Gazda, 2015; Da Costa et al., 2018; Aspesi and Ellis, 2019), whose defining characteristics include reduced proliferation and increased apoptosis of erythroid progenitor cells, raising the possibility that proteotoxic stress could contribute to the manifestation of DBA (Recasens-Alvarez et al., 2021).
evidence: This describes the connection between RPG mutations and DBA, citing five references.

claim: Proteotoxic stress could contribute to the manifestation of Diamond-Blackfan anemia.
source: Moreover, it is well established that mutations in around 20 different RPGs, mostly leading to haploinsufficiency of individual r-proteins, result in the development of a ribosomopathy called Diamond-Blackfan anemia (DBA) (Narla and Ebert, 2010; Danilova and Gazda, 2015; Da Costa et al., 2018; Aspesi and Ellis, 2019), whose defining characteristics include reduced proliferation and increased apoptosis of erythroid progenitor cells, raising the possibility that proteotoxic stress could contribute to the manifestation of DBA (Recasens-Alvarez et al., 2021).
evidence: This is a speculation about the role of proteotoxic stress in DBA, citing Recasens-Alvarez et al., 2021.

claim: Several unassembled r-proteins interact with the E3 ubiquitin ligase MDM2 and thereby inhibit the ubiquitination and degradation of the apoptosis-promoting transcription factor p53.
source: Further, several unassembled r-proteins, especially RPL5 and RPL11 in the context of the 5S RNP but also RPL4 and RPL26, whose yeast counterparts are established Tom1 targets (Sung et al., 2016a; Sung et al., 2016b), interact with the E3 ubiquitin ligase MDM2 and thereby inhibit the ubiquitination and degradation of the apoptosis-promoting transcription factor p53 (Bursac et al., 2014; Pelava et al., 2016).
evidence: This describes the interaction between r-proteins and MDM2/p53, citing four references.

claim: Both overexpression and depletion of RPL4 lead to p53 stabilization.
source: In the case of RPL4, both its overexpression and depletion, the latter in an RPL5- and RPL11-dependent manner, lead to p53 stabilization (He et al., 2016).
evidence: This describes the effect of RPL4 levels on p53, citing He et al., 2016.

claim: A possible connection between RPL3 and RPL4 variants and DBA is suggested by the identification of missense mutations in RPL3 and RPL4 in DBA patients.
source: Moreover, a possible connection between RPL3 and RPL4 variants and DBA is suggested by the identification of missense mutations both in RPL3 (one DBA patient; His11 to Arg substitution, unknown significance for disease manifestation) and RPL4 (one individual with DBA-like phenotypes; Val-Leu insertion between Ala58 and Gly59) (Gazda et al., 2012; Jongmans et al., 2018).
evidence: This describes mutations in RPL3 and RPL4 found in DBA patients, citing two references.

claim: Increased p53 activity plays a pivotal role in eliciting tissue-specific defects in a variety of different developmental syndromes.
source: Besides in DBA, increased p53 activity also plays a pivotal role in eliciting tissue-specific defects in a variety of different developmental syndromes (Bowen and Attardi, 2019).
evidence: This describes the role of p53 in developmental syndromes, citing Bowen and Attardi, 2019.

claim: Genetic changes in HUWE1, encoding the ortholog of Tom1, are associated with multiple neurodevelopmental disorders, prominently including X-linked intellectual disability.
source: In this respect, it is worth mentioning that genetic changes in HUWE1, encoding the ortholog of Tom1, are associated with multiple neurodevelopmental disorders, prominently including X-linked intellectual disability (Giles and Grill, 2020), and that reduced HUWE1 levels, due to a disease-causing mutation, increase p53 signaling (Aprigliano et al., 2021).
evidence: This describes the connection between HUWE1 mutations and neurodevelopmental disorders, citing two references.

claim: Reduced HUWE1 levels, due to a disease-causing mutation, increase p53 signaling.
source: In this respect, it is worth mentioning that genetic changes in HUWE1, encoding the ortholog of Tom1, are associated with multiple neurodevelopmental disorders, prominently including X-linked intellectual disability (Giles and Grill, 2020), and that reduced HUWE1 levels, due to a disease-causing mutation, increase p53 signaling (Aprigliano et al., 2021).
evidence: This describes the effect of HUWE1 mutations on p53 signaling, citing Aprigliano et al., 2021.

claim: Individuals with mutations in CNOT1 exhibit a broad range of neurodevelopmental phenotypes, most consistently resulting in intellectual disability, development, speech, and motor delay, and hypotonia.
source: Moreover, individuals with mutations in CNOT1 exhibit a broad range of neurodevelopmental phenotypes, most consistently resulting in intellectual disability, development, speech, and motor delay, and hypotonia (Vissers et al., 2020).
evidence: This describes the phenotypes associated with CNOT1 mutations, citing Vissers et al., 2020.

claim: Perturbed proteostasis, elicited by unassembled r-proteins such as RPL3 and RPL4, could contribute to the development of DBA and possibly influence the aging process and be of relevance to the etiology of diverse developmental disorders and neurodegenerative diseases.
source: Taking into account the findings of our study and the above considerations, perturbed proteostasis, elicited by unassembled r-proteins such as RPL3 and RPL4, could not only contribute to the development of DBA but possibly also influence the aging process and be of relevance to the etiology of diverse developmental disorders and even neurodegenerative diseases of protein aggregation (Kaushik and Cuervo, 2015; Szybińska and Leśniak, 2017; Maor-Nof et al., 2021).
evidence: This is a speculation about the broader implications of the study's findings, citing three references.
